title: Normalized finite-coefficient Cartier agreement maps
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum $k,\ell,E,n\geq1,A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions], and the prescribed twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Let $a:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a $k$-scheme and $i:D\hookrightarrow T$ an effective Cartier divisor [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Put $W=T\setminus D$, $N=\ell^n$ and $R=\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z$. With $i_*$ the etale direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and $\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{N,T}\otimes_R A$ the etale finite root line of [def-pur-frame-kummer-class], define $c^e_{D,A}:i_*A_D\to(\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{N,T}\otimes_R A)[2]$ to be the ordinary etale component of the uniquely normalized Cartier Kummer family of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map], at coefficient level $n$ and annihilating exponent $N$. Define $c_D:i_*A_D\to A_T(1)[2]$, an element of the pro-etale supported Hom group $H^2_i(T,A(1))$ of [def-pur-supported-class-operations], to be its image under the canonical etale-to-pro-etale supported-Hom comparison $\operatorname{cmp}_i^{2,1}$ of [def-pur-supported-hom-site-comparison]. The source comparison preserves the constant quotient, and the target comparison is the roots-projection identification of [def-pur-frame-class].

The named $c_D$ has the explicit normalization of its source's relative-torsor construction: put $N=\ell^n$, $R=\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z$, take the relative Kummer boundary of the frame torsor of $(\mathcal O_T(D),s_D|_W)$, realize it as $b_D:i_*R_D\to\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{N,T}[2]$ via [lem-amb-closed-support-hom], apply derived scalar extension $-\otimes_R^L A$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], and then the canonical etale-to-pro-etale and supported-source comparisons and the roots-projection target identification of [def-pur-frame-class]. This specifies the constructed morphism referred to by that name.

source.place: Relative frame-torsor class, supported Kummer boundary, derived scalar extension, and roots-projection comparison; the c_D normalization paragraph of lem-pur-cartier-class-agreement

Neither definition uses the agreement theorem. The normalization is the second paragraph of lem-pur-cartier-class-agreement; no declaration is duplicated.
